Subject: Marketplace product copy: CTA & trial visibility + SKU mapping

Hi Olga,

We're putting the final assets together for our AWS Marketplace product page and wanted to get Redwood's sign-off on a couple of tricky spots before we submit. Attached is a short one-pager with proposed hero copy and the current SKU/pricing layout (product_onepager.pdf). High-level things we need help on: 

- CTA phrasing: should the primary CTA be "Start free trial" or "Request private offer"? AWS rules around trials + Private Offer overlap and we don't want customers to click the wrong thing.
- Trial visibility: we plan to offer a 14-day trial via Private Offer for enterprise prospects, but the listing will show a trial badge — does that create a mismatch?
- SKU mapping: our usage tiers map to different AMIs/entitlements; we need guidance on how to display this without confusing buyers.
- Co-sell assets: any specific copy or badge copy recommended for co-sell qualification?

Can you route this to whoever owns marketplace copy at Redwood and let us know recommended hero/CTA text and a short note about how to represent the Private Offer trial in the product page? If easier, I can join a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Claire
Product Lead, Summit Retail
attachments: product_onepager.pdf

Subject: Re: Marketplace product copy: CTA & trial visibility + SKU mapping

Thanks, Olga and Claire — I sketched two short hero variants and a recommended CTA strategy below. My goal: minimize clicks and reduce buyer confusion while keeping procurement flows intact.

Hero variant A (enterprise-first):
- Headline: "High-throughput inference for retail personalization"
- Subhead: "Predictable latency and cost across hosted and private deployments"
- Primary CTA (button): "Request Private Offer (14-day trial)"
- Secondary CTA (link): "View pricing & usage examples"

Hero variant B (self-serve emphasis):
- Headline: "Ship LLM features with consistent performance"
- Subhead: "Start with a free test instance or contact us for enterprise pilots"
- Primary CTA (button): "Start free trial"
- Secondary CTA: "Contact sales"

Recommendation: Use Variant A if Summit wants to prioritize enterprise procurement and co-sell readiness — this sets expectations that trials will be handled via Private Offer and surfaces co-sell. Variant B is better if Summit expects many self-serve signups.

SKU + Pricing notes:
- Show 3 public usage tiers on the main page (Basic / Starter / Enterprise).
- Under "Technical details" include a collapsible section "AMI & entitlements" that lists mapping (AMI-xyz -> Starter; AMI-abc -> Enterprise). Call out that AMI availability depends on Private Offer entitlements.

Copy snippet for Pricing footnote (short):
"Enterprise trials and private procurement are available via Private Offer. Contact the vendor for entitlement and AMI access"

Co-sell badge language (short):
"Co-sell eligible — contact us for joint engagement"

Related links: DocuSign for co-sell MOU: https://docusign.com/EXAMPLE-MOU (placeholder)
Seller Central preview: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/listing/EXAMPLE-1234

If you want, Marissa and I can assemble a one-page listing-ready text block and push it back by EOD. Olga — would you prefer we go async or book the 30-min?

—Kimberly
Head of Marketplace Programs
Redwood Inference
